newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak, seen lower.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak, seen lower.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended weak on Wednesday as the market tested but failed to climb above a key technical barrier ahead of the March contract's expiry.
Dealers said activity was driven by players rolling over their positions to the June contract before March's settlement on Thursday.
"Most of the trades were rollovers. People were selling the spreads. I don't think anybody was putting on new positions," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
The Nikkei 225 March contract ended 120 points easier at 18,105 after testing a high of 18,325 on volume of 17,170 lots. June lost 135 points to 18,055 on 22,760 lots.
"The 18,300 resistance has been quite strong so I guess the market's going down from here," said the trader, adding, however, that support at the 17,800 level was likely to hold this week.
He said the Nikkei's failure to make any headway after the dollar breached 122.30 yen also suggested a weak undertone.

Dealers said reports of merger talks between Japan Telecom Co Ltd and International Telecom Japan Inc and Ajinomoto Co's disclosure that two of its officials had been arrested for suspected involvement in illegal deals weighed on the market.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 349.9 against its opening 350.0 on volume of 343 lots. April finished at 346.1 against 345.0 on 451 lots.
